G0406.name: Andrew
G0406.desc: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
G0406.short: Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ and played a significant role in the early church.

G0408.name: Andronicus
G0408.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G0408.brief: Fellow prisoner with Paul, outstanding among the apostles
G0408.short: Andronicus, along with Junia, was a fellow prisoner with Paul and was noted as outstanding among the apostles.

G0451.name: Anna
G0451.desc: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
G0451.brief: Prophetess who witnessed Jesus' dedication in the temple
G0451.short: Anna, a prophetess and widow, witnessed the dedication of the infant Jesus in the temple and spoke about Him to all who were looking forward to the redemption of Jerusalem.

G0452.name: Annas
G0452.desc: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
G0452.brief: High priest during Jesus' ministry and trial
G0452.short: Annas, a high priest, played a significant role in the events surrounding Jesus' arrest, trial, and crucifixion, as well as in the early persecution of the apostles.

G0493.name: Antipas
G0493.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G0493.short: Antipas, described as Christ's faithful witness, was martyred in Pergamum, where Satan's throne was said to be.

G0490H.name: Antioch
G0490H.brief: A city in Pisidia where Paul preached the gospel.
G0490H.short: Antioch in Pisidia, a city visited by Paul on his missionary journeys.
G0490H.meaning: “city of Antiochus,” named for the Seleucid king

G0490G.name: Antioch
G0490G.brief: A major city where the gospel spread to Gentiles.
G0490G.short: Antioch, a city in Syria where the gospel first reached Gentiles and the believers were first called Christians.
G0490G.meaning: “city of Antiochus,” named for the Seleucid king

G0494.name: Antipatris
G0494.brief: A city where Paul was taken during his transfer to Caesarea.
G0494.short: Antipatris, a city where Paul was brought by soldiers during his journey to Caesarea.
